From: Samira Qureshi <ops@brightleaf.io>

Cc: Brightleaf SRE <sre@brightleaf.io>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 429s during bulk ingestion - Brightleaf

Hi Diego,

We started a scheduled bulk import of HR transcripts this morning around 08:30 PT and within ~10 minutes many of our ingestion jobs started receiving 429s from Redwood’s API. The errors are intermittent but enough to cause backpressure in our pipeline; we've queued retries but it's causing timeouts downstream.

Attached is a filtered snippet of the ingestion logs showing request IDs and timestamps (ingestion-log-20270320.txt).

Questions:
- Is this a customer-side rate cap I'm hitting or did something change on your end?
- Can you temporarily increase our rate while we finish the job?

We’re on an urgent push to complete this migration by EOD. Please advise next steps and any mitigation you can apply quickly.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Qureshi
Head of Platform Ops, Brightleaf Health
ops@brightleaf.io

--

Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s during bulk ingestion - Brightleaf

Hi Samira — thanks for the heads up and the logs.

We’re looking into this now. Initial triage notes:
- The ingestion trace shows bursts of concurrent short-lived sessions from Brightleaf during the 08:30–08:45 window that aligned with our enforcement window change earlier this morning.
- It looks like a quota-window translation issue where your tenant mapping hit a stricter enforcement bucket (per-tenant token window) rather than your higher committed burst window.

Immediate actions:
1) I’m authorizing a temporary burst override for your tenant to avoid additional 429s while we patch (effective ~5m).
2) Neha will coordinate a config patch to correct the window mapping and push a targeted rollback of the enforcement change for your account.
3) Ben will prepare a short runbook for your SREs with retry/backoff guidance and a suggested ingestion cadence to avoid re-triggering enforcement.

We’ll follow up in this thread with an ETA. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll make this right.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s during bulk ingestion - Brightleaf

Hi all — update from the ops side.

Root cause (short): a recent enforcement-window config change was deployed to streamline tenant mapping. A translation edge case caused Brightleaf’s tenant to be associated with a per-minute token bucket (tight window) instead of your agreed burst window, so short concurrent sessions hit 429s during bursts.

What we did:
- Applied a hotfix to the mapping service to restore the correct burst window for Brightleaf (patch id: map-fix-20270320).
- Applied a temporary override to your tenant to surface the higher burst capacity for the next 24 hours while we validate.
- Added a short runbook (patch-runbook-429.pdf) with recommended ingest pacing and the precise header to set for higher burst-aware routing.

Follow-ups planned:
- Ben will run a replay test of your ingestion pattern in a staging environment to confirm no further 429s.
- We’ll ship a more robust validation in the deployment pipeline to prevent this mapping regression.

ETA: we expect normal behavior to be restored and validated by 14:30 PT today.

Neha Kapoor
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability
